newsitem.title: USA: American Stock Exchange to replace composite index.
newsitem.headline: American Stock Exchange to replace composite index.

text.p: The American Stock Exchange said it will introduce a new AMEX Composite Index, replacing the widely used index currently employed by the exchange.

The exchange said the new index is a price appreciation index, which brings it into conformity with other major indices. The current AMEX Composite is a total return indicator, which includes dividend reinvestment in addition to simple price appreciation.
The index's symbol will be .XAX on Reuters terminals, replacing the current symbol .XAM.
The AMEX said it will provide data on the new composite starting with December 27, 1995 for purposes of historical comparison.

The exchange also said it will introduce five sub-indices to track market sector performances: information technologies .XIT ; financial .XFI ; healthcare .XHL ; natural resources .XNA ; and industrials .XID.
The AMEX's current industry and geographic sub-indices are being discontinued on December 31, 1996.
